CausalChain: Hypoxia → HIF activation → Upregulation of PHGDH (activating SSP) and CD73 → Increased NADPH production (antioxidant capacity) and adenosine accumulation → Reduced ROS and immune cell dysfunction → Enhanced survival and drug resistance in HCC; therefore, simultaneous blockade of SSP and adenosine pathway would reverse both intrinsic (tumor cell) and extrinsic (immune) resistance.
Hypothesis: Dual targeting of the HIF‐induced serine synthesis pathway and adenosinergic metabolism can overcome therapeutic resistance in hypoxic hepatocellular carcinoma by re‐sensitizing tumor cells to TKIs and restoring anti‐tumor immune responses.
Abstract: Hypoxia‐inducible factors (HIFs) drive metabolic reprogramming in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through activation of glycolysis, lactate metabolism and the serine synthesis pathway (SSP), along with concomitant upregulation of adenosinergic enzymes. This metabolic reprogramming not only facilitates tumor cell survival under oxidative stress but also contributes to immune evasion. Here we hypothesize that HIF‐mediated activation of the SSP and adenosine production, through upregulation of PHGDH and CD73 respectively, concurrently supports both intrinsic drug resistance in tumor cells and immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment. Consequently, dual inhibition of the serine synthesis/folate cycle axis and adenosine signaling may synergistically overcome resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in hypoxic HCC.
